Unit Tests for Java Code (using Junit):
```java
import org.junit.*;
public class EntryTest {
    @Test public void testGetLengths() {
        // Arrange - create an instance of a tested object in the environment to be worked upon by tests → no external setup required here as we don't have any input data, just objects created and used within methods. The objective is simply that it builds with minimal setups (Arrange) before performing action/assertion(Act).
        Entry entry = new Entry("TestKey",new long[]{12345678L},null); // Act → we want to test the GetLengths method, so pass in a key and an array of lengths. Let's assume that this works correctly for now as it is not being used anywhere else at present
        Assertions.assertEquals("  12345678",entry.GetLengths()); // Assumption: Entry object was initialized with the expected length, so we check if method returns correct lengths string by comparing actual and expectation → no external setup required here as it is a test that should not depend on any other tests or data outside of its scope
    }  
}```
Unit Tests for C# Code (using Nunit):
